The key risk is whether markets can be convinced this divergence is sustainable.
quote: I think today was a great example that the answer is yes. And I think if you get this sort of turn in the yield curve that they're attempting to orchestrate, Maybe not in a coordinated way, but that's certainly been the result. The curve has flattened because Beasant has successfully held back the long end, while the front end has rallied on Walsh's supposed hawkish ness. What that's allowing them to do is essentially maintain containment of break even rates, while at the same time keeping term premium relatively contained. And so what's going on at the front end can be essentially divorced from the back end. What this ends up looking like is a decline in real rates that ultimately benefits call. So this can create a situation where real rates are up. But the longer term break evens or not, that's very much a gold positive story.
